posts.title: Explore or exploit?
posts.description: The core dilemma of reinforcement learning. Your favourite restaurant, or something new tonight? That's the multi-armed bandit problem. Watch three diners find out who ends up happiest, and how AI agents learn the same way.

posts.title: Self-Organizing Maps (SOMs)
posts.description: A visual guide to how Self-Organizing Maps organize high-dimensional data into a 2D map without labels: neuron competition, the Best Matching Unit (BMU), neighborhood learning and topology preservation.

posts.title: Regression vs. Classification: what are we trying to predict?
posts.description: If the target is a continuous value, use regression; if it is a category or class, use classification. Regression → How much? Classification → Which one?

posts.title: Why are small engineering datasets different?
posts.description: Engineering data is expensive and hard to scale. A small engineering dataset brings limited coverage, higher uncertainty, noise and a greater risk of overfitting, so engineering ML needs careful data collection, domain knowledge, uncertainty assessment and proper validation.

posts.title: Is AI in engineering here to replace physics?
posts.description: AI and machine learning can accelerate calculations, discover patterns and support better decisions, but physics remains the foundation of accurate, trustworthy engineering models. Physics + AI → Better Engineering.

posts.title: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs)
posts.description: How does a neural network remember the past? A visual guide to how RNNs carry information through time with a hidden state: sequential data, recurrent connections, BPTT, vanishing gradients and the motivation behind LSTM and GRU.

posts.title: What does a Machine Learning model actually see?
posts.description: A model doesn’t see the real world, it sees a representation of it: Real World → Data → Features → Model → Prediction. Understanding this pipeline is a first step toward understanding how ML works.

posts.title: AI Foundations 02 | Data, Features, Labels & Samples
posts.description: The building blocks of machine learning: how real-world observations become model inputs as data, samples, features and labels, and why data quality matters more than simply having more data.

posts.title: AI × Engineering 01: CFD Surrogate Models
posts.description: A deeper look at AI × CFD: where machine-learning surrogate models can add value and, more importantly, when we can trust their predictions.

posts.title: Can AI replace CFD in engineering?
posts.description: CFD and AI are not competitors: they can work together to build faster, more efficient engineering workflows.

posts.title: Will AI replace humans? Or transform the way we work?
posts.description: The future may not be Humans vs. AI, but Humans + AI. The real advantage will be learning how to work with AI.

posts.title: Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP)
posts.description: How does an MLP actually learn? A visual guide that organizes the core concepts behind the learning process of a multi-layer perceptron.

posts.title: How does a machine actually learn?
posts.description: At its core, machine learning is an iterative loop: Data → Model → Prediction → Loss → Update → Better Model. The model predicts, measures the error, adjusts its parameters and repeats.

posts.title: AI Foundations 01 | Understanding Artificial Intelligence
posts.description: What do we actually mean by Artificial Intelligence? A simple journey from intelligent behavior and rule-based systems to machine learning, deep learning, learning from data, generalization and reliability.
